newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt offers 20pct stake in state cotton ginnery.
newsitem.headline: Egypt offers 20pct stake in state cotton ginnery.

text.p: Egypt on Wednesday offered investors at least 20 percent or 1.2 million shares in state-run firm Nile Cotton Ginning.

In a published advertisement, the state's Holding Company for Cotton and International Trading fixed the minimum share price at 42 pounds a share and said the final share price would be based on what investors bid at.
Investors can buy a minimum 10,000 shares and the deadline for submitting bids is 1900 GMT on January 26.
Nile Cotton Ginning has a total capital of 29.44 million pounds based on 5.888 million shares worth a nominal five pounds.
Apart from ginning cotton, the firm refines and processes vegetable oils and also manufactures ghee and cooking fat.
The advertisment showed that Nile Cotton Ginning almost doubled net after-tax profits for the 1995/6 financial year to 14.089 million pounds ($4.14 million) from 7.187 million in the previous year.
The financial year ends on June 30.
Net sales also rose to 54.625 million in 1995/6 from 40.863 million in 1994/5.
Investors must accompany their bids with a valid check for two percent of the total amount they want to pay. Banque Misr is handling the sale.
